First, the levels a player has beaten today are meant to be marked on that list, and they are not. After beating levels 1 to 3, all 20 rows look exactly alike, and only the one line "Best: level 3" higher up says how far the player got. Once built, each beaten row carries a "Beaten" badge beside the Commander and Checkpoint badges the rows already have. Second, a player reading in Chinese sees four of the twelve Commanders, the bosses of levels 5 and 10, named in English ("Redline, the Overclocked", say) on the list, the briefing, the fight and the replay list, while the Commander's own cards, listed under that English heading, are already named in Chinese. On about eight days in nine at least one of the day's Commanders is one of these four. Once built, every Commander is named in Chinese, and a test fails when a later Commander, enemy or doctrine arrives without its Chinese words, before any player sees English. ## Why - **Beaten levels.** §16.7 (`spec/16-infinite-assault.md:115`) asks for the ladder with "those beaten today and the checkpoints marked". The checkpoints are marked (a `Checkpoint` badge, `apps/web/src/assault/day/DayScreen.tsx:104`); the beaten levels are not. Their only cue is `data-beaten` on the row (`DayScreen.tsx:100`), coloured by `.assault-ladder > li[data-beaten="true"]::marker` (`apps/web/src/assault/assault.css:50-53`). But `.assault-ladder > li` is `display: grid` (`assault.css:43-48`), and browsers generate a `::marker` only for a `display: list-item` box, so that rule draws nothing: no row shows a marker at all, beaten or not. No test can see it: `DayScreen.test.tsx` never sets a beaten level, and `e2e/cypress/e2e/59-assault.cy.ts:87-89,171-172` checks only the attribute, which is there. - **Commander names.** `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` has no entry for "Echo-1, First Hallucination" or "Redline, the Overclocked" (rank I), nor for "Loopback, Who Returns" or "Root Kit, the Exploiter" (rank II), all four in `crates/run/src/assault.json:53-57` and shipped through `assault_catalog_content`. A Commander level's enemy is the Commander's name (`crates/run/src/assault/day.rs:248-250`), and `t()` hands it back untouched: the only pattern keys whose shape would match ("{first}, {second}", "{label} {n}") have fewer than `MIN_PATTERN_WORDS` words of their own and answer only their own calls (`apps/web/src/i18n/i18n.ts:114,137-140`). The name shows in English at `DayScreen.tsx:102`, `Briefing.tsx:46` and `:52`, `FightScreen.tsx:253` (the rail, the enemy hero and the replay label) and `routes/replays.tsx:100` and `:266`. Each rank's Commander is drawn uniformly (`day.rs:163-171`), so level 5 is in English on two days in three, level 10 likewise, and at least one of them on eight days in nine. - **Why the check missed it.** `i18n.test.ts:268`, "R711000 every table-fed sentence has a zh-CN entry", says "A new table feeding `t()` joins this walk". The Assault's content reaches `t()` only through variables (enemy, Commander, doctrine name and line), and it never joined the walk. Extending that walk is the check for this miss (CLAUDE.md rule 15), not a new rule. ## Proposal 1. In `DayScreen.tsx`, a beaten row (`level.level <= record.best`, as today) gets a visible `t("Beaten")` badge in the style of the Commander and Checkpoint badges; `data-beaten` stays for the e2e spec. Remove the ladder's half of the dead `::marker` rule (the upgrades list's half sits on plain list items, works, and stays). Add zh-CN entries for "Beaten" and the four Commander names, each built on its card's Chinese name so a briefing's heading and the card list under it agree. 3. In `i18n.test.ts`'s table-fed walk, push every value the Assault's content feeds to `t()`: each doctrine's name, line and enemies, and each Commander's name, read through `assaultContent()` from `wasm/index.ts` as `writing.test.ts:297` already does. ## Where it lands - `apps/web/src/assault/day/DayScreen.tsx`, `apps/web/src/assault/assault.css` - `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` - `apps/web/src/assault/day/DayScreen.test.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/i18n.test.ts`; optionally `e2e/cypress/e2e/59-assault.cy.ts:171`, to check the badge's words beside the attribute - SPEC §16.7 (`spec/16-infinite-assault.md:115`) as written: no spec change and no new ruling. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] With today's record at best 2, the day screen's rows for levels 1 and 2 show "Beaten" and the row for level 3 does not; the `DayScreen.test.tsx` test that asserts it fails on `main`. - [ ] No `::marker` rule remains on `.assault-ladder > li`. - [ ] `zh-CN.json` holds "Beaten", "Echo-1, First Hallucination", "Redline, the Overclocked", "Loopback, Who Returns" and "Root Kit, the Exploiter". - [ ] The table-fed walk in `i18n.test.ts` includes every Assault doctrine name, line and enemy and every Commander name; on `main` it fails naming the four missing names, and with the entries it passes. - [ ] `pnpm -C apps/web test src/assault src/i18n/i18n.test.ts` and `pnpm -C apps/web typecheck` pass. ## Size and risks Small: about five files, a dozen lines of code and tests, and five dictionary entries.
